title: add-data-zone-claim-propagator-and-kms-proof-middleware
author: Maya Chen
body: Context: Customers with strict data residency requirements have asked for a lightweight, gateway-level enforcement that propagates a tenant's declared data-zone claim through the call chain, attaches a verifiable KMS-origin proof to encrypt/decrypt calls, and records compacted, integrity-checked audit metadata. This PR implements a middleware chain that (1) validates incoming data-zone claims in service tokens, (2) injects a signed KMS-origin header for downstream services, and (3) emits a compact audit envelope optimized for high-throughput paths. Motivation: existing enforcement lived deep in the policy enforcer and was costly to evaluate per-request; it also duplicated audit payloads and made post-facto verification expensive. Design summary: - DataZoneClaimPropagator: reads tenant-level claim from request context (Authorization JWT or tenant metadata header) and canonicalizes it to a single header X-Redwood-DataZone. If a request is missing an explicit claim, the propagator applies the customer's pinned-region default from tenant metadata; if no default exists the request is marked with X-Redwood-DataZone=unknown and flagged to the audit pipeline. - KMSProofMiddleware: for requests that require KMS-bound operations, the middleware attaches X-Redwood-KMS-Proof which is a compact signature (ed25519) over request id + data-zone + timestamp. The service uses a short-lived signing key derived from the operator's KMS identity; the middleware delegates to the existing kms-client interface for key lookup and signing. - AuditCompactEnvelope: replaces the verbose audit JSON for high-throughput endpoints with a CBOR-encoded envelope that contains a stable fingerprint, sequence id, and a digest of the full JSON audit payload stored asynchronously in the audit store. This drastically reduces per-request logging bandwidth while preserving verifiability and replay protection. Backwards compatibility: the middleware adds both the new compact envelope header (X-Redwood-Audit-Env) and preserves the existing full-audit outbound call in the background for 30 days behind a feature flag (audit.compact_rollout). Rollout plan: stage rollouts by route (default: text-gen heavy paths first) with a canary at 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%. Include a kill-switch at service config (feature flag + operator override) to revert to previous auditing behavior immediately. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for propagator normalization and fallback rules - [x] Integration tests that exercise KMS proof creation and verification (local kms mock) - [x] Audit compact envelope roundtrip tests (encode/decode and digest verification) - [x] Load test to validate added middleware latency < 1.5ms p50 on our benchmark-lab profile - [x] Security review with cryptography team completed - [x] Linear -> SUP ticket linking for support ops docs Changeset summary: - server/middleware/data_zone_propagator.go: new middleware, 150 LOC - server/middleware/kms_proof.go: new middleware that calls kms-client.SignCompact - audit/compact/envelope.go: encoder/decoder + digest helpers - cmd/rollouts/feature_flags.yaml: introduces audit.compact_rollout flag and canary config - docs/security/data-zone-claims.md: added operational documentation - test/integration/kms_proof_test.go and audit_compact_test.go - minor updates to existing policy-enforcer to read X-Redwood-DataZone when evaluating geofence rules Tests and CI: CI initially failed due to a flaky kms-client mock timeout in integration (CI run #342); fixed by increasing mock timeout and adding retry in test harness; subsequent CI run passed. Observability: added metrics: middleware.data_zone.propagated_total, middleware.kms_proof.signed_total, audit.compact.bytes_saved_estimate; added tracing spans for the propagator and kms proof sign step. Security considerations: - Signing keys are ephemeral and must be rotated by KMS; code ensures keys are not materialized in process except as ephemeral in-memory signatures. - Fallback 'unknown' data-zone is treated as highest-sensitivity by policy-enforcer to avoid accidental residency violations. - Audit compact envelope uses SHA-256 digest; the full audit payload is stored into the existing encrypted audit store, and the digest is included in the envelope to allow later retrieval and verification. Deployment notes: - Requires a coordinated rollout with edge gateways so X-Redwood-DataZone is honored across service boundaries. - Ops must enable kms signing key injection in the KMS policy for services; added a playbook steps in docs/security for tenant ops. - Feature flag default is off and will be enabled per-customer after acceptance testing. Related work: ties into ENG-2029 (RBACv2 policy reads of propagated claims) and SUP-4321 (customer support runbook for pinned-region misreports).

review_comments: Ibrahim Noor (2026-02-27): Please ensure the KMS proof header cannot be replayed. Can we include a monotonic sequence id from the request router?
Maya Chen (reply 2026-02-27): We include request id+timestamp and the signing key is short-lived; added a sequence id field to the envelope per request-router contract in commit c3378a5.
Priya Sethi (2026-02-28): The propagator fallback to tenant default is fine, but add a test for when tenant metadata is malformed. Also please document operator steps for key provisioning.
Maya Chen (reply 2026-02-28): Added malformed metadata test and extended docs with key provisioning steps.

Liam O'Connor (2026-03-01): CI flaky test observed earlier; thanks for the timeout fix. One concern: audit.compact_rollout default off for all services? Suggest default off for other regions until we validate storage dedupe behavior.
Maya Chen (reply 2026-03-01): Agreed — kept default off and added per-region gating in feature_flags.yaml; will coordinate with infra for canary in us-west-2 first.
release_notes: Introduces DataZone claim propagation middleware, compact KMS-origin proofs for downstream verification, and an audit compact envelope to reduce logging bandwidth on high-throughput paths.
Rollback: feature flag audit.compact_rollout=false or disable at service config to restore previous auditing behavior.
